resources.string: Emufii: Azahar and Eden netplay filling
Lets Emufii fill in the connection address in Azahar\'s or Eden\'s multiplayer menu, so you don\'t have to retype it. Emufii only watches those two emulators, and only while a session is running.
Filters the library as you type, across every console.
Grid, carousel or list. The list is the one that tells two dumps of a game apart.
A → Z, recently added, or by console: sorting by console files the library into folders.
Open sessions, to join with a code or a keypress.
Your friends, who is online, and the session they are playing.
Your name, your avatar and your friend code. And every app setting.
Pick the folder your ROMs are in. Subfolders are scanned too, whichever console they hold.
It won\'t show in the session list: people will need your code to get in.
It will show in the session list, where anyone can join it.
The game opens on its own
You play online, nothing to set up
Emufii opens a session and gives you a code
Your friends type it in to join you
The consoles see each other as on local Wi-Fi
You play with strangers, on a public server run by third parties. Emufii creates no session and brings up no tunnel: it opens PPSSPP, and PPSSPP is what connects you.
To do, once and for all
First exit any running PSP game to PPSSPP’s menu. Then use the button below and go to Settings → Networking.
Turn networking on, and pick a public server from the list PPSSPP keeps up to date.
Leave “Try to use the server’s packet relay” on Automatic: that is what public servers want. Emufii switches this game back to private-session values automatically when needed.
Come back here and launch the game, then take its ad hoc mode.
1. Open PPSSPP to set up online play
Allow Emufii to install apps in your Android settings.
This version isn\'t downloadable here yet.
Download interrupted. Try again, the file is there.
File rejected: it isn\'t signed like this app.
Emufii creates no session: this mode does not go through it.
Emufii opens PPSSPP for you to set up, then the game, in that order.
In the game, take ad hoc mode: you land among the players already connected.
Share it, or let your friends find you in the open sessions.
DS online play doesn\'t go through a session
Multiplayer isn\'t supported for this console yet
DS online play starts from the library, not from a session
No ROM attached to this session
Choose PPSSPP’s memory-stick folder in Emufii Settings first.
Android no longer grants Emufii read and write access to PPSSPP’s memory stick. Choose the folder again in Settings.
This is not PPSSPP’s memory-stick root. Choose the folder that contains PSP/SYSTEM/ppsspp.ini.
Emufii cannot find this dump’s PSP DISC_ID. Keep the ID, such as ULUS10277, in a compressed game’s filename or use an ISO/PBP dump.
Launch affected games in public mode before changing PPSSPP’s folder, so Emufii can restore their original network settings.
PPSSPP’s game configuration could not be written and verified.
Emufii opens multiplayer and fills the address in for you.

Before you play, set your name by hand in Azahar → Settings and system: it needs at least 5 characters. Emufii leaves it alone, and Azahar refuses the room when the name is too short, blaming the address, which is fine.
Open the menu → Multiplayer, then enter %1$s.
Emufii can no longer reach the session server: the player list below is from the last answer we got. The tunnel itself is holding: a game already running keeps running. Check your connection.
You\'re in the session and on the same network, but Emufii couldn\'t find this game on your device. Add it to your ROMs folder, rescan, then come back.
In PPSSPP, once and for all
PPSSPP cannot be driven by Emufii: it draws its own interface. These four settings are yours to make, once, and never again.
Emufii will apply PPSSPP’s four private-session network values for this game immediately before launching it. Everything else, including your nickname, stays yours.
Automatic PPSSPP setup is ready, launch the game.
Before switching between a private session and public play, exit the running game to PPSSPP’s menu. PPSSPP can otherwise save the old in-memory values over the new ones.
Networking → Ad hoc server address → Add server → paste %1$s
Just below it: “Try to use the server’s packet relay” set to Disabled
PPSSPP says so itself: that mode is for when a public server relays packets for you. Here your consoles talk to each other directly: it has nothing to do.
Networking → Enable built-in ad hoc server
System → Nickname: yours, Emufii never touches it

This is the one setting that really changes how the game feels, and it is not in the emulator. Measured on a real match: a player sitting far from their router sends packets in bursts instead of a steady stream, and it shows up on screen as stutter. Same player, closer in, and it is gone. Prefer 5 GHz over 2.4, and turn power saving off.
This address never changes: the relay sends it to whoever is hosting your session, game after game.
You both need the exact same version of the game, updates and DLC included. A version that differs on one side stops the game, usually without saying why: the room joins, then nothing starts.
Eden\'s multiplayer lives in its settings, not in the game: ⚙ Settings → Multiplayer → “Create”. You can open it before or during play.
Eden\'s multiplayer lives in its settings, not in the game: ⚙ Settings → Multiplayer → “Join”. You can open it before or during play.
Emufii fills the address, the port and your nickname in for you as soon as the dialog opens.
Your Emufii nickname is copied into Eden: two players with the same nickname cannot share a room, and Eden gives everyone the same one by default.
DS online play doesn\'t work by session: each console dials the revival server, there is no network to share. Go back to the library and start the game from there.
The game is in your library, but Emufii doesn\'t know how to set up multiplayer for this console yet. The session network is up: go ahead if your emulator can make use of it.
No open sessions. Start yours from your library and it will show up here for everyone else.
This can take 10-15 s the first time.
Your photo stays on your phone. Other players see your initials and your colour.
What everyone else sees in the session.
Subfolders are scanned too, whichever console they hold.

Emufii sets up remote multiplayer between emulators: it shares a network, it doesn\'t reimplement any game. Distributed under the AGPL 3.0 licence, it never routes to Nintendo\'s official servers and ships no ROMs, no BIOS and no keys.
Emufii can fill the address into the emulator\'s multiplayer menu, so you have nothing to copy out.
Emufii cannot fill the emulator\'s form in. Sessions still work, the address just has to be typed by hand.
Android can switch it off on its own, after an update or a change of device. This is where it goes back on.
Too many attempts, try again in a minute
Without VPN permission, Emufii cannot bring the network up
Session not found, the code may have expired
Emufii can\'t reach its server. Check your connection and try again.
This session is for %1$s. Join it with that game.
The host has not finished connecting
Without VPN permission, Emufii cannot join
DS online play is holding the tunnel, and Android allows only one. Continuing will cut the redirection to Kaeru: a DS game in progress would be interrupted.
A session is still open and holding the tunnel, and Android allows only one. Continuing will close it.
The previous tunnel did not stop

Nintendo\'s servers have been off since 2014. Kaeru WFC is a third-party reimplementation that replays the original protocol. Emufii points melonDS\'s lookups at it, and nothing else on the device is affected.
Kaeru isn\'t answering, the game won\'t be able to connect
Without the VPN the console will go to Nintendo\'s dead servers
Session tunnel status for remote multiplayer
DNS redirection for DS online play
This build of %1$s (%2$s) has no multiplayer. Update it to play online.
This is the name your friends will see. Emufii also hands it to the emulator when it connects you to a game.
%1$d characters minimum: emulators reject a shorter name.

Play online with your friends, on the emulators you already have. Emufii puts your devices on one network: the games believe you are sitting side by side, and their local multiplayer runs across the internet.
Emufii shows the tunnel and local network status in a notification while you play inside the emulator. Without it, Android may cut the network when Emufii goes to the background.
Declined. You can turn it on later in Android\'s settings.
Give this code to someone so they can add you. It never changes, unless you reset your profile.
That code isn\'t valid. Check you copied all of it.
Swap codes with someone: you\'ll then see when they\'re playing, and join them in one tap.
Remove %1$s from your friends? You\'ll need their code to add them back.
Your friends list stays on your phone. The server only knows who is online, and forgets it after two minutes.
Delete your profile? This can\'t be undone: your friend code changes, and your friends list is erased.
If you use Cocoon or ES-DE, Emufii can take the artwork you already have there, including the ones you re-cropped yourself. No key, no download: your games wear the face you gave them.
A ROM holds only a 32 or 48 pixel icon. With a SteamGridDB key, Emufii fetches real box art for the games Cocoon does not cover.
Free key at steamgriddb.com, in your account preferences. Without it, the ROMs\' own icons stay.
No icon for this game. Try another name: matching uses the file name, which isn\'t always the game\'s.
The game leaves Emufii\'s library. The file and its saves are untouched, and the settings bring everything back.
Removed games stay on your storage: only their tile is gone. Restoring puts them all back in the grid, in alphabetical place.
Inside Emufii only: the file on your storage is left alone. Leave empty to restore the original title.
Search a game, a player, a code
Open the room, then pick the game inside it: everyone starts it together.
Join the room, then wait for the host to pick the game. Do not start anything yourself.
You both need the exact same dump. Dolphin compares hashes and refuses otherwise.

You also need to start from the same save. If one of you is further along, the two games diverge the moment they start: each player sees a different match, with no error message. Safest is for neither of you to have a save at all.
Emufii fills in the address and port, sets the connection to direct, and points the room at the session\'s game.
In Dolphin, ⋮ menu then Netplay: direct connection, and enter %1$s.
The PS2 network profile is missing. Open Emufii\'s settings, "PS2 network profile": without it, no PS2 LAN game will open its local menu.
The PPSSPP setup is missing. Open Emufii\'s settings, "Automatic PPSSPP setup": without it, a PSP session never joins the game\'s ad hoc lobby.
The saved folder is unavailable or no longer writable.
Preserving the original card in slot 2…
Enable automatic filling: Emufii needs it to assign the card through ARMSX2\'s real settings.
This is not the root of ARMSX2\'s custom folder: the memcards subfolder is missing.
Android did not grant permanent read and write access to this folder.
The automation never started. Turn Emufii\'s accessibility service off and back on in Android settings, or set the emulator up by hand.

%1$s is a folder memory card: it cannot carry the network profile, and the BIOS browser shows it as empty, so nothing can be copied out of it by hand. Emufii created a new card for slot 1 and copied %2$d save(s) from %1$s onto it. Your original folder is left untouched.
%1$s is a folder memory card. Emufii created a new card for slot 1 and copied %2$d save(s) onto it, but %3$d did not fit: a PS2 card holds 8 MB. Your original folder is left untouched.
%1$s is a folder memory card, and it is empty. Emufii created a new card carrying the network profile for slot 1. Your original folder is left untouched.
%1$s is not a usable PS2 memory-card image. The original was not modified.
%1$s changed while it was being copied. Close the running game in ARMSX2 and try again; no incomplete clone was published.
Several BIOS/NVM pairs are possible (%1$s). Select the active BIOS in ARMSX2, then prepare again.
The NVM for %1$s is visible but its BIOS is not, so Emufii will not guess the i.Link offset.
Could not read ROMVER from %1$s. No incompatible profile was produced.

resources.string: In the game, pick LAN, System Link or Network Play. You are the one opening the match.
Wait for the host to open their match, then join it from the game\'s LAN menu.
Only games that shipped with a LAN or System Link mode work here, around sixty in all. If the game asks you to sign in to a server, it was an online game, and Emufii cannot help with it.
With the network adapter attached, some games stop responding to the controller entirely. If that happens, turn DEV9 Ethernet off in ARMSX2.
When you launch, Emufii configures DEV9, Local Link, the room and the network card for this game, then opens it directly. No ARMSX2 navigation is needed.
In ARMSX2, Settings then Network: local mode, and enter %1$s.
This image does not expose a readable boot CRC. Emufii opened ARMSX2 only to assign the prepared card. Return here afterward and press setup again for the network fields.
This image does not expose a readable boot CRC, so it needs the legacy ARMSX2 fallback. Enable automatic filling in Emufii settings, then try again.
Turn a console off to take it out of your library, with its games.
Proven at the versions shown here.
Shows the session code on the rear panel, while Emufii is in the foreground.
No second screen detected on this device.
Nothing is known about this game yet.
When a friend comes online or starts a game.
When a new version of Emufii is available.
Open the app to install it.

Emufii tells you when a friend comes online or starts a game, and when a new version is out. Outside the app an alert can arrive up to a quarter of an hour late: with no push service, Android only wakes the app at intervals.
Azahar runs the games. Emufii raises the tunnel, opens its lobby and fills it in for you.
A session code is all your friend needs: their console sees yours as if on local Wi-Fi.
Azahar has to be a pre-release: the latest stable build has no multiplayer screen.
Eden runs the games, and the room is raised on Emufii\'s own server: nobody hosts on their console.
You both join it, and the session code is its password.
PPSSPP looks for an ad hoc server at one fixed address; the relay points it at the session\'s host.
Public online play does not go through Emufii at all: PPSSPP connects on its own, no session, no tunnel.
Nintendo\'s servers have been off since 2014, so melonDS goes to Kaeru WFC, which reimplements them.
No session and no code: Emufii redirects the game\'s requests and you meet whoever is already there.
Without the redirection running, the console calls the dead servers and finds nobody.
ARMSX2 runs the games. Emufii opens the session, then hands you the address and port to type into the game\'s network menu.
The network profile lives on a memory card in slot 1; Emufii prepares it and brings your saves over to it.
Without that profile, no PS2 LAN game will open its local menu.
Dolphin runs the games, and its own Netplay is what carries the match.
Emufii raises the tunnel and puts you in the same lobby; the session code is what your friend types.
Both players must launch exactly the same dump, or Dolphin refuses the match.
ROM folder, artwork, keys, hidden games
What to set up outside Emufii
Pick PPSSPP\'s memory-stick root: the folder holding PSP/SYSTEM/ppsspp.ini. Android grants access to that one only.
Before a private session, Emufii writes the per-game network settings PPSSPP understands.
A public launch puts back whatever was there before.
Leave a running PSP game to PPSSPP\'s menu before switching modes.
Pick ARMSX2\'s custom folder. Emufii finds the memory card and the BIOS in it.
Emufii prepares a checked card carrying the network profile: a copy of yours where possible, otherwise a fresh card holding a folder card\'s saves.
At launch it is assigned to the chosen game only. No save is ever deleted.
Subfolders are scanned too, whichever console they hold.
Second folder, scanned along with the first.
What shows up in the grid
The session closes for everyone and the tunnel comes down. A game already running keeps going.
You leave the session and the tunnel comes down. A game already running keeps going.
The friends list is on the second screen
This is taking longer than usual. The tunnel or the server may not be answering.
Pick how to start the game on the front screen.
You can change it any time in Settings → Profile.
Emufii reads your ROMs where they already are. It never moves them, renames them, or writes inside them.
Tap Choose folder: Android\'s picker opens.
Find the folder holding your games, then confirm with Use this folder.
Emufii looks inside subfolders too. Keep your usual filing, consoles mixed together if you like.
Emufii will look for your games as soon as you are done. Expect a few seconds, even for several hundred.
Pick the consoles you actually play. The others stay out of your library, and we won\'t bother you with their setup.
You can change your mind any time in Settings → Consoles.
Your frontend has already downloaded real artwork for your games. Emufii can read it straight from there: no account, no key, no network.
Go to Android → data → Cocoon\'s folder (Cocoonv2), then confirm.
Go to the ES-DE folder at the root of your storage, then confirm. Its downloaded_media folder also works.
Emufii only reads images there. It never writes into %1$s\'s folder.
Emufii will prefer %1$s\'s artwork. Only a picture you chose yourself comes ahead of it.
Without a frontend, your games show only the tiny icon tucked inside the ROM. A free SteamGridDB key replaces it with real box art.
Create an account on steamgriddb.com, it is free.
Open your account preferences, API section, and generate a key.
Paste it below. It is only used to look up images, and stays on this device.
PPSSPP won\'t take an address from outside. Emufii has to write it into PPSSPP\'s own files before every game, hence the folder to point out, once.
PS2 asks for a network profile
Just like on the real console, PS2 games look for their network settings on the memory card. Emufii installs a profile there once, and you never touch it again.

Before every game, the emulator asks for the host\'s address and port, to be typed in by hand. Allow this and Emufii fills them in for you. It only ever sees the screen of the emulator it is filling in.
Tap Allow: Android asks the question.
Answer Allow. This is what keeps the tunnel up while you play.
During a game, a notification shows the tunnel\'s state and the session code.
Your library opens next. Point at a game and press B to launch it, or start a session to play it with someone.
Everything you skipped is waiting in Settings, with the same explanations.
